questions.problem:
Given that $A$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 5$ matrix, and $C$ is a $5\times 3$ matrix, in which of the following expressions are the Hadamard products well-defined?

I. $AB⊙C$

II. $AB⊙{C}^{T}$

III. $(AB)^{T}⊙C$
questions.worked_solution:
The Hadamard product of two matrices (or vectors) is only defined if they have the same dimensions.

Let's consider each expression in turn:

- The dimensions of $AB$ are $3\times 5,$ and the dimensions of $C$ are $5\times 3.$ Hence, the Hadamard product in expression I is *not* well-defined.

- The dimensions of $AB$ are $3\times 5,$ and the dimensions of ${C}^{T}$ are $3\times 5.$ Hence, the Hadamard product in expression II is well-defined.

- The dimensions of $(AB)^{T}$ are $5\times 3,$ and the dimensions of $C$ are $5\times 3.$ Hence, the Hadamard product in expression III is well-defined.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".

Let's consider each expression in turn:

- The dimensions of $YX$ are $4\times 4,$ and the dimensions of ${Z}^{T}$ are $4\times 4.$ Hence, the Hadamard product in expression II is well-defined.

- The dimensions of $(XY)^{T}$ are $2\times 2,$ and the dimensions of $Z$ are $4\times 4.$ Hence, the Hadamard product in expression III is *not* well-defined.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

$$ A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]. $$ Given the matrices above, write the following expression as a Hadamard product. Here $(\,\cdot \,)$ denotes matrix multiplication.
$(AB)\cdot (By)=\,\,$ $3$ $⊙$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}} {{field-3}}
questions.worked_solution:
The Hadamard product of two compatible vectors $u$ and $v$ can be expressed as the matrix product

$$
v⊙u=\text{diag}(v)u.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
By=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}(AB)\cdot (By) & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\text{diag}([\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}])[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]⊙[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
For compatible matrices $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ and scalar $\alpha ,$ the Hadamard product has the following properties:

- Commutativity:

$$
A⊙B=B⊙A
$$

- Associativity:

$$
(A⊙B)⊙C=A⊙(B⊙C)
$$

- Distributivity over Addition:

$$
A⊙(B+C)=A⊙B+A⊙C
$$

- Scalar Distributivity:

$$
\alpha (A⊙B)=(\alpha A)⊙B=A⊙(\alpha B)
$$

In this case, by the commutativity of the Hadamard product, we have

$$
(Q⊙P+R⊙P)-{X}^{T}=(P⊙Q+P⊙R)-{X}^{T}.
$$

Then, by the distributivity over the addition of the Hadamard product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(P⊙Q+P⊙R)-{X}^{T} & =P⊙(Q+R)-{X}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 & -5 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6-4 & -2-(-5) \\ 1-0 & 3-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
